correctness.rationale: Finite Fourier positivity is exactly two-variable linear inequalities for the real-even symmetrization. An explicitly factored globally positive polynomial has only the two pentagonal zeros. Five-divisibility gives matching dual upper bound, and nondivisibility permits strict scaling. Eventual two-contact coefficients follow from a nonzero first-order determinant. Uniform positivity away from the zeros and strict curvature at both zeros establish feasibility on all grid sites. Two asymptotically positive dual weights prove optimality and real-even uniqueness; an explicit Taylor calculation gives the precise O(N^-3) residue correction. Reproduced 5190 deterministic checks corroborate the algebra but do not substitute for the proof.
